bihar_raw_news.title: 5.3-Magnitude Earthquake Rocks Nepal, Tremors Felt Across Parts of Bihar - Republic TV
bihar_raw_news.content: Updated 24 November 2026 at 08:05 IST There were no immediate reports of casualties or significant damage to property following the earthquake. Authorities are expected to assess the situation and monitor any developments in the affected areas. Namya Kapur World News 2 min read Follow : 5.4-Magnitude Earthquake Rocks Nepal, Tremors Felt Across Parts of Bihar | Image: X A 5.4-magnitude earthquake struck Nepal's Koshi Province on Tuesday, November 24, triggering tremors that were reportedly felt in several districts of Bihar, raising concerns among residents across the region. According to the European Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC), the earthquake struck Nepal at a depth of approximately 10 kilometres. The relatively shallow depth of the earthquake may have contributed to the shaking being felt in areas beyond its epicentre. Residents in parts of Bihar reportedly experienced tremors, prompting some people to step out of their homes and buildings as a precautionary measure. However, details regarding the exact districts affected and the intensity of the tremors in Bihar were not immediately available. There were no immediate reports of casualties or significant damage to property following the earthquake. Authorities are expected to assess the situation and monitor any developments in the affected areas. Advertisement Nepal, located in the seismically active Himalayan region, is particularly vulnerable to earthquakes due to the ongoing collision between the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates. The region has witnessed several significant seismic events over the years, including devastating earthquakes that caused widespread destruction and loss of life. The latest earthquake comes as a reminder of the seismic vulnerability of Nepal and neighbouring parts of India, particularly Bihar, which shares a long border with the Himalayan nation. Advertisement Residents have been advised to remain cautious and follow safety guidelines in case of further tremors. Disaster management authorities continue to monitor the situation for any updates regarding damage, casualties or aftershocks.

national_raw_news.title: HM Amit Shah says, development of Northeast & employment generation for young people remains...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that the development of the Northeast and employment generation for young people remains a top priority for the Narendra Modi government. Launching four major development initiatives worth more than 5,610 crore rupees in Arunachal Pradesh, Mr Shah said the Centre is working to strengthen infrastructure and improve access to essential services in the region, especially in villages along the international border. Highlighting the Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP), he said the government has changed the perception of border settlements from the country’s “last villages” to its “first villages”, underscoring their strategic and developmental importance. Mr Shah noted that the programme was initially taken up in villages in Arunachal Pradesh along the China border. He said, Mobile Medical Units have also been deployed across 11 border districts, equipped with telemedicine facilities, AI-based portable tuberculosis screening, digital X-ray machines, ECG equipment and modern laboratories. Home Minister said the Northeast has witnessed significant improvements in connectivity over the past 12 years, with the region’s state capitals now connected through rail and air services. He also highlighted the expansion of road, railway, air and waterways infrastructure. Calling for greater economic self-reliance in Arunachal Pradesh, the Home Minister urged the state to strengthen local production of milk, eggs, meat and fish. The initiatives launched yesterday include Mission Shikshit Arunachal – Phase II, Chief Minister’s Comprehensive State Power Development Programme, and Chief Minister’s Comprehensive State Rural Road Development Programme. In addition, 199 projects under the Vibrant Villages Programme are being taken up across 11 border districts. Shah also launched Mission SURAKSHA.

national_raw_news.title: Ten films to compete for ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at IFFI 2026
national_raw_news.content: Ten films will compete for the prestigious ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa this year. The award recognises films that reflect Mahatma Gandhi’s ideals of non-violence, tolerance, intercultural understanding and a culture of peace. The ten films selected for this year’s competition bring together stories from diverse cultural backgrounds, highlighting human relationships, social challenges and shared values. Akashvani correspondent reports that the ten films selected for this year’s competition explore a wide range of contemporary social realities, including gender inequality, human relationships, social justice, compassion, friendship and the challenges of a rapidly changing world. India is represented by three films – Sarfaraz Alam’s Kabir Sir ka Akhri Lesson, Kannan S.’s Scroll and Muskan Asthana’s Sev Micchar. Among today’s highlights, Turkish filmmakers Faysal Soysal’s Rahma and Elif Ada’s The Farm will be screened. Among other films that will be screened during the nine-day festival are Emily Atef’s Call Me Queen, Gessica Généus’s Marie Madeleine, Amartei Armar’s Our Time Will Come, Laïla Marrakchi’s Strawberries, and Lu Po-Shun’s Will You Still Be My Friend. The four-member international jury, headed by Algerian filmmaker and film critic Professor Ahmed Bedjaoui, will adjudicate the entries. Through this showcase, IFFI reinforces cinema’s ability to go beyond entertainment and become a powerful medium for dialogue, empathy and social change – values that lie at the heart of the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal.

national_raw_news.title: Jammu & Kashmir: 10-day Jhiri Mela to begin today 4 hours ago 71
national_raw_news.content: In Jammu and Kashmir, the 10-day Jhiri Mela, which is celebrated at Jhiri village in Marh block on the outskirts of Jammu city, will begin today. Held annually in honour of Baba Jitto and Bua Kodi, the Mela draws pilgrims and visitors from the Jammu region and neighbouring states, including Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Himachal Pradesh. This Mela is associated with the supreme sacrifice of 16th-century Dogra hero and revolutionary, and honest farmer, Baba Jitto, who was a great devotee of Mata Vaishno Devi. This event is a platform to promote local craftsmen and highlight traditional arts for visitors from beyond J&K. The event is vital not only for local agriculture but for showcasing Jammu’s cultural heritage. This fair promotes unity, honesty, truthfulness, courage and innocence in society and signifies the rich culture of the region. Akashvani correspondent reports that Baba Jito fought against injustice and laid down his life after he was cheated by the landlord of the area, sacrificing his life for justice and righteousness. Pilgrims come to Jhiri village to pay tributes to Baba Jitto. The Mela is anticipated to attract about 15 lakh visitors, making it an opportunity for government departments to actively promote schemes and programmes that benefit rural populations. Various Government departments have set up specialised kiosks to provide information on relevant government schemes, ensuring farmers’ welfare remains central. This event is a platform to promote local craftsmen and highlight traditional arts for visitors from beyond Jammu & Kashmir and is vital not only for local agriculture but for showcasing Jammu’s cultural heritage. Agriculture department displays are planned with mushroom cultivation blocks (button, Dhingri, Cordyceps, Shiitake), hybrid vegetable seedlings, honey varieties, a millet restaurant, plant health services, and farmer scheme showcases. Enhanced efforts have been made by the administration to educate attendees, especially farmers, about agricultural advancements, available seeds and fertilisers. All arrangements are in place for the event, including infrastructure upgradation, blacktopping of all main and link roads, rejuvenation and improved accessibility to Bawa Talab, sanitation, public safety and reasonable pricing of farming tools, etc at the event. Besides, plans for crowd management, parking, health services and uninterrupted water and electricity supply reaffirm the administration’s commitment towards making this year’s Mela a memorable and impactful event.

national_raw_news.title: Actors appreciate IFFI for bringing diverse stories and cinematic perspectives from India and across the world
national_raw_news.content: Actor Salil Acharya has appreciated the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) for bringing together diverse regional and international cinema on a common platform. Talking to Akashvani News in Goa, he said that the festival offers an opportunity to discover films from different countries and understand the diverse emotions and creative perspectives behind filmmaking. He observed that cinema should be appreciated beyond box-office collections and also expressed pride in the growing global reach of Indian cinema. Talking to Akashvani News, actor, casting director and producer Palash Dutta appreciated the Festival theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, saying that cinema brings people together beyond cultural and geographical boundaries. A regular visitor to IFFI for the past 10 to 12 years, Dutta said this year’s festival offers a unique blend of stories from different parts of the world. Odia actor Archita Sahu expressed happiness over the gala premiere of her film Baghuni (Dance Like a Tiger) at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Talking to Akashvani News, she said the film highlights Bagha Nacha, Odisha’s traditional folk tiger dance, while addressing themes of equality and dignity. The film also seeks to draw attention to the preservation of this traditional art form.

national_raw_news.title: Kalai-II dam project's flawed clearances expose risks of fast-tracking SUMP
national_raw_news.content: Kalai-II dam project’s flawed clearances expose risks of fast-tracking SUMP — The Arunachal Times [email protected] Monday, 23 November 2026 [email protected] The Arunachal Times The Arunachal Times Monday, 23 November 2026, 12:17 am arunachaltimes.in State News Monday, 23 November 2026, 12:17 am • 5 min read Kalai-II dam project’s flawed clearances expose risks of fast-tracking SUMP [Badak Yomgam] On 8 April, 2026, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs cleared an investment of Rs 14,105.83 crore for the 1,200 MW Kalai-II Hydroelectric Project on the Lohit River in Arunachal Pradesh’ Anjaw district. An official Press Information Bureau (PIB) release framed the venture as a landmark step for clean power and regional connectivity. Planned as a 78-month run-of-the-river project, comprising six 190 MW units and one 60 MW unit, and executed through a joint venture between THDC India Limited (a public sector subsidiary of NTPC Limited) and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the Kalai-II dam is designed to generate 4,852.95 MU of electricity annually, strengthen state’s power supply, manage peak demand, and balance the national grid. Under the central package, Arunachal is slated to receive 12 percent free power plus one percent earmarked for the Local Area Development Fund, alongside Rs 599.88 crore in budgetary support for enabling infrastructure, Rs 750 crore in central financial assistance towards the state’s equity share, and roughly 29 kilometres of new roads and bridges in Anjaw and Namsai districts, largely accessible for local use. Yet, looking beyond official projections to ecological reporting and local accounts exposes severe environmental and social costs that threaten the Lohit basin. An investigative report first published on Mongabay on 19 June, 2026, detailed how the proposed dam site in Hawai, located just 26.5 kilometres from the Namdapha Tiger Reserve and 11 kilometres from the Kamlang Wildlife Sanctuary, sits directly inside the Eastern Himalaya biodiversity hotspot and requires felling 33,338 trees across tropical wet and dense mixed forests. Beyond potential noise and water pollution, wildlife experts warned of serious risks to endemic and sensitive species such as the takin (for which the environmental impact assessment proposes a Rs 100 lakh conservation plan covering habitat protection, anti-poaching, monitoring, research, training, and awareness), the large Indian civet, the Assamese macaque, and the jungle cat. Most critically, the project endangers the white-bellied heron, a critically endangered bird listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act. With fewer than 60 individuals estimated globally in 2015 and only six to nine remaining in Arunachal, the species depends on clear, shallow, fast-flowing river streams to forage for fish and struggles to adapt when river habitats are altered. The urgency of protecting the Lohit’s riverine habitat was brought into sharp focus on 12 November, 2026, when the white-bellied heron research team of the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) recorded a sighting of the bird along the Lohit River, noting that fewer than 10 individuals are believed to survive in the wild in India, and that undisturbed Eastern Himalayan riverine habitats are vital to its survival.
